content: Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the likelihood of severe side effects. It is essential to maintain a comprehensive list of all the products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications can influence the elimination of aprepitant from your body, potentially affecting its efficacy. Examples of such drugs include azole antifungals (e.g., itraconazole, ketoconazole), diltiazem, macrolide antibiotics (e.g., clarithromycin, erythromycin), nefazodone, HIV protease inhibitors (e.g., nelfinavir), rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin), and ritonavir. Aprepitant itself can either accelerate or slow down the removal of other medications from your body, which may impact their effectiveness. If you are taking warfarin, aprepitant may alter how well warfarin works in your system. Additionally, this medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. It is advisable to discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use a reliable backup birth control method while taking this medication and for one month after your last dose. Aprepitant is closely related to fosaprepitant. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. If you miss a dose of this medication, it is crucial to consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Do not attempt to double up on doses without professional guidance. Store the capsules at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing them in the bathroom. The liquid form of this medication should be refrigerated and any unused liquid discarded after 72 hours. Do not freeze the liquid. When ready to use, the liquid form may be kept at room temperature for up to three hours. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not encompass all possible details about this product.
